content.overview: Section 172 is the residual penalty provision for Chapter XI (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors). If a company contravenes any of the provisions of this Chapter and no specific penalty or punishment is provided elsewhere, the company and every officer of the company who is in default are liable to a penalty as specified in the section.
content.glance: Residual penalty for Chapter XI contraventions where no specific penalty is provided; company and every officer in default are liable.
content.study: If a company contravenes any of the provisions of this Chapter and for which no specific punishment is provided therein, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty as provided in the section (as in force). Where a provision of the Chapter has its own specific penalty (for example section 159 for certain DIN defaults), that specific penalty applies and section 172 is not used as a substitute. Current-law framing: identify the Chapter XI provision breached; check whether a specific penalty exists; if not, apply s. 172 to company and officers in default.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies to contraventions of Chapter XI (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) for which no specific penalty is provided.

sections.heading: Who Is Liable
sections.body: The company and every officer of the company who is in default.

sections.heading: Residual Character
sections.body: Where a section in the Chapter has its own penalty, that penalty governs; s. 172 fills the gap only when none is provided.

examples.title: No specific penalty
examples.body: A Chapter XI duty is breached and the particular section states no penalty of its own. Section 172 supplies the residual penalty for the company and officers in default.

examples.title: Specific penalty exists
examples.body: A DIN default falls under section 159. The specific penalty in s. 159 applies; s. 172 is not used in place of it.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 172 override a specific penalty in another section of the same Chapter?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 172 applies only where no specific punishment is provided for the contravention. Specific penalties take priority.

distinctions.title: Residual Chapter penalty (s. 172) vs specific DIN penalty (s. 159)
distinctions.left: Gap-filler for Chapter XI where no specific penalty exists
distinctions.right: Specific penalty for defaults under ss. 152, 155 and 156

misconceptions.trap: Section 172 is the only penalty provision for all director-related breaches.
misconceptions.correction: Many sections have their own penalties. Section 172 is residual and applies only when no specific penalty is provided.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 172 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify Chapter XI provision breached. II. Check for a specific penalty. III. If none, apply s. 172 to company and officers in default. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Provision breached; absence of specific penalty; defaulting officers; precise relief.

examTips: Residual only — check for specific penalty first.
